decisions.context: The brief sets the system’s quality priorities but no explicit latency, cost, or scale targets.
drivers: Reproducible forecasts for any past week
Get model ideas to production quickly

chosen.label: Use these four requirements as ADR drivers

decisions.rationale: Historical reproducibility is the top requirement; release safety and iteration speed follow. Team size makes operational simplicity relevant.

decisions.context: The pipeline must produce weekly forecasts reliably while allowing the team to change models. Manual coordination is possible but places each run’s consistency on the team.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
pros: Weekly run safety: repeatable connected stages
cons: Small team: orchestration adds setup and upkeep

alternatives.label: Manual script-driven workflow
pros: Small team: low initial tooling burden
cons: Weekly run safety: depends on manual consistency
Fast iteration: coordination slows repeat runs

decisions.rationale: Weekly run safety decides: an orchestrated pipeline makes stages repeatable and easier to rerun as model ideas change. This accepts added orchestration upkeep; “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describe connected, repeatable stages.
consequences: Pipeline stages and dependencies need maintenance.
Changes can be evaluated through a repeatable workflow.

decisions.decision: How should historical forecasts be reproducible?
decisions.context: Recreating a forecast for a past week requires the team to recover the relevant data and model context, not just the model artifact. The brief makes this a system requirement.

alternatives.label: End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance
pros: Historical reproducibility: tracks datasets, runs, and artifacts
Weekly run safety: preserves lifecycle context
cons: Small team: metadata process needs upkeep

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Historical reproducibility: omits full data and run context

decisions.rationale: Historical reproducibility decides: tracking dataset versions, pipeline definitions, dependencies, and run metadata supports reconstructing past forecasts. This costs metadata upkeep; “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support lifecycle traceability.
consequences: Each run needs linked data, code, configuration, and artifact versions.
The team must preserve historical inputs and metadata.

decisions.decision: How should model releases protect the weekly run?
decisions.context: New model ideas need a route to production that does not jeopardize the established weekly forecast. A release should be reversible if it causes problems.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
pros: Weekly run safety: enables rollback after a bad release
cons: Small team: release stages and rollback need upkeep

alternatives.label: Unified release automation
pros: Fast iteration: automates build and release
cons: Weekly run safety: rollback is not explicit

decisions.rationale: Weekly run safety decides: progressive promotion with rollback limits the impact of a faulty model release. This adds release process upkeep; “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” describe staged deployment and restoration.
consequences: Previous production versions must remain available.
Promotion stages need clear validation and rollback criteria.

decisions.decision: How should candidate models be evaluated before promotion?
decisions.context: The brief encourages new model ideas but requires the weekly run to remain dependable. Candidates need evaluation before they replace the current production model.

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Weekly run safety: evaluates candidates before deployment
Fast iteration: repeatable comparison against held-out data
cons: Historical reproducibility: requires maintained evaluation data

alternatives.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
pros: Fast iteration: compares candidate models by metric
cons: Weekly run safety: standalone metric comparison does not establish a release gate

decisions.rationale: Weekly run safety decides: evaluating candidates on held-out data before deployment helps prevent an unchecked model change from affecting production. This requires maintaining evaluation data; “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describe evaluation before model selection or deployment.
consequences: Held-out evaluation data and criteria must be maintained.
Candidate evaluation becomes part of the release workflow.

uncovered: How to set forecast accuracy targets and business-specific evaluation metrics.
How long to retain historical input data and run artifacts.
How to monitor forecast quality and trigger retraining or rollback.
